units.function: Unit tests extracting a trimmed legacy plan body from custom plan tags embedded in Issue descriptions.
units.dependencyDirection: Unstructured legacy Issue text flows into a document migration helper and yields nullable Markdown body.
units.keyDataModels: Issue description string, plan tag block and extracted Markdown.
units.lifecycle: No or whitespace-only block yields null; one populated block is trimmed and returned.
units.testAssessment: Basic absent/populated/empty cases are covered. Missing are multiple/nested/malformed/case-varied tags, very large input, code fences containing tags, Unicode and migration idempotency/provenance.
units.designRationale: Recover structured plan content from a former inline storage representation.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS will need explicit, reversible migrations when Work/evidence/document schemas evolve.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the compatibility-reader approach only; use versioned serializers, provenance and migration receipts rather than HTML-like delimiters in core data.
units.responsibilityConflict: Extracted prose has no author, version or evidence digest, so it cannot independently establish an approved plan.

units.function: Unit tests deriving a unique display name by comparing normalized Project shortnames and appending increasing numeric suffixes.
units.dependencyDirection: A proposed Project name and in-memory list of existing IDs/names enter a pure naming helper; an optional excluded ID supports updates.
units.keyDataModels: Project ID/name, normalized shortname, numeric suffix and excluded Project ID.
units.lifecycle: Unused or non-normalizable names remain unchanged; collisions produce Name 2, Name 3, while the updated Project can be excluded.
units.testAssessment: Core collision cases are clear. Missing are database races/unique constraints, locale/Unicode/case normalization, existing numeric suffixes, length limits, reserved names and large-list complexity.
units.designRationale: Preserve human-friendly names while generating routable unique short identifiers.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS organizations/projects/workspaces need stable opaque IDs plus optional human slugs that can change safely.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the UX behavior; make opaque ID canonical and enforce slug uniqueness transactionally per organization with explicit locale-neutral normalization and conflict retry.
units.responsibilityConflict: Automatic renaming is presentation behavior and must not alter the stable identity used in responsibility or evidence records.

units.function: Unit policy tests deciding whether Issue checkout should wake an Agent assignee or suppress a redundant self-wakeup inside an active Run.
units.dependencyDirection: Actor type/Agent, checkout Agent and Run identity enter a pure route policy and produce a scheduler wake boolean.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor type, actorAgentId, checkoutAgentId, checkoutRunId and wake decision.
units.lifecycle: Board checkout wakes; an Agent checking itself out in an identified active Run does not; missing Run identity or acting for a different Agent wakes.
units.testAssessment: The four truth-table branches are covered. Missing are authorization, stale/completed Run IDs, duplicate wake idempotency, concurrent checkout, Agent aliasing, cancellation and scheduler delivery evidence.
units.designRationale: Avoid recursive or duplicate heartbeat scheduling when the executing Agent itself claims its Work.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS Connector execution needs idempotent wake/resume semantics that distinguish an active attempt from a new external assignment.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT as one rule inside a versioned Work scheduler state machine using attempt IDs and an outbox; do not infer execution state from actor equality alone.
units.responsibilityConflict: Wake suppression says nothing about who authorized checkout or whether the active Run owns the Work contract and current lease.

units.function: HTTP regression proving SPA fallback rereads index.html so deployments do not serve stale hashed asset references.
units.dependencyDirection: Every fallback request synchronously reads a Web build directory through a branding helper and returns no-cache HTML.
units.keyDataModels: Static index path, hashed asset URL, HTML response and Cache-Control.
units.lifecycle: After index.html changes on disk, the next deep-link request receives the new asset hash rather than a cached old document.
units.testAssessment: The stale-deploy regression is covered, but missing are missing/partial files, atomic deployment swaps, sync-I/O performance, cache validators, CSP/security headers, brand injection escaping and immutable asset caching.
units.designRationale: Keep a long-lived server process aligned with newly replaced frontend artifacts.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS independent Web deployments need safe rolling upgrades and cache coherence across managed and self-hosted profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the no-stale-index invariant; use atomic versioned releases, immutable assets, no-cache index with ETag and deployment smoke tests rather than synchronous disk reads per request.
units.responsibilityConflict: This is delivery plumbing and provides no release provenance or accountable promotion record by itself.

units.function: Unit tests for MCP HTTP request headers and parsing buffered JSON or SSE-framed JSON-RPC responses.
units.dependencyDirection: Caller headers flow through a protocol helper that forces MCP Accept semantics; untrusted response body/content type flows into a parser returning an unvalidated object.
units.keyDataModels: Content-Type/Accept/Authorization headers, JSON-RPC id/result, SSE event/data frames and content type.
units.lifecycle: Requests advertise JSON and SSE despite caller Accept overrides. Responses parse plain JSON or collect multiline SSE data, skip non-RPC events and return a JSON-RPC-like message; missing data throws.
units.testAssessment: Useful compatibility tests cover JSON, SSE, ping skipping, multiline data and empty streams. Missing are streaming/backpressure, body/event/line limits, timeout/cancel, malformed UTF-8/JSON/SSE, multiple responses, request-ID correlation, jsonrpc/error schema validation, content-type spoofing, header injection and Authorization redaction.
units.designRationale: Interoperate with MCP servers that use either immediate JSON or SSE transport while preserving required protocol negotiation.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS Connectors may use MCP internally, but the control plane requires bounded, vendor-neutral tool events and cannot trust raw protocol payloads.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT inside an MCP-specific Data/Tool Connector with a streaming parser, strict limits, schema and request-ID validation, cancellation, redaction and normalized evidence envelopes. Do not expose MCP types in core/application.
units.responsibilityConflict: A syntactically parsed JSON-RPC response is not execution evidence; it lacks tool permission, data scope, responsible Work/approval digest and runtime attestation.
